To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) we provide a truthful approximation algorithm for the generalized assignment problem in a setting where agents have private valuations, (2) we show that the approximation factor is tight and (3) we show that a similar result does not hold in a setting where the agents have public valuations.

(i) the problem of computing an optimal solution is APX-hard; (ii) the problem of approximating the optimal solution is AP-approximable; and, (iii) a truthful approximation mechanism can be designed for the strategic GAP problem.

(i) we propose truthful mechanisms for GAP without money; (ii) we prove that the approximation factor of our mechanisms is tight; (iii) we show how to compute the mechanisms' approximation factors in polynomial time; and (iv) we show that the approximation factors of our mechanisms can be improved in polynomial time.
